collection.label: Virgil: the golden age and the return of souls
collection.author_name: Virgil (70-19 BCE); Vergilius Romanus and Vergilius Vaticanus (4th-5th century)
collection.search_terms: virgil vergil fourth eclogue golden age sibyl new race messianic aeneid book 6 anchises world soul spiritus intus alit lethe elysium vergilius romanus vaticanus
collection.description: Virgil's fourth Eclogue, on the return of the golden age, and Anchises' account of the world-soul and the return of souls in Aeneid 6, on the two oldest illustrated manuscripts of Virgil.

texts.title: Virgil, Eclogue 4: the return of the golden age
texts.source: Vat. lat. 3867 (Vergilius Romanus) fol. 9v-11r (DigiVatLib) + Greenough Latin (Perseus) + James Rhoades (1921) English (Perseus)
texts.description: Virgil's fourth Eclogue, written around 40 BCE: the last age foretold by the Sibyl has come, the Virgin returns and a new race is sent down from heaven, and a child is born under whom the iron age will end and the golden age return. Shown on the Vergilius Romanus (5th century).

texts.title: Virgil, Aeneid 6.724-751: Anchises on the world-soul and the return of souls
texts.source: Vat. lat. 3225 (Vergilius Vaticanus) fol. 55r-55v (DigiVatLib) + Greenough Latin (Perseus) + Theodore C. Williams (1910) English (Perseus)
texts.description: In the underworld Anchises explains to Aeneas that one spirit and mind move the whole universe, that souls have a fiery heavenly origin dulled by the body, and that after purification they drink of Lethe and return to bodies. Shown on the Vergilius Vaticanus (about 400).
